Subject: Service assurance: minimum uptime & monthly credit construct

Hi Maya,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. As we start working through the commercial and legal checklist for the FinApps integration, procurement asked me to capture our ask and get a draft SLA back for review. Two items are top of mind for our CFO and platform team:

1) Minimum monthly uptime — Finance is pushing for an industry-standard baseline (they suggested 99.9%), and want to understand the crediting mechanism if we fall below that.
2) Latency commitments — our product needs predictable p95 latency for inference calls (target: p95 < 300ms for the hosted API). If a separate dedicated tier is required for that guarantee, please call it out.

Other constraints:
- Scheduled maintenance windows should be clear and carveouts called out.
- Credits should be simple to reconcile on the monthly invoice (we prefer a single credit line).

Could you share a short proposal (high level bullet points) and an editable SLA draft we can circulate with legal? Ideally we’ll have something to review by the end of the month.

Appreciate it —
Sabrina

Hi Sabrina —

Thanks — we can absolutely get a clean draft over. High-level proposal below, and I attached a working SLA draft (redwood_sla_draft_v3.pdf) with editable sections for credit bands and maintenance carveouts.

Quick summary (hosted API):
- Standard uptime floor: 99.95% monthly (measured per calendar month).
- Monthly credit bands (applied as a percentage of services fees for that month):
  * 99.95% - 99.80%: 5% credit
  * 99.79% - 99.50%: 15% credit
  * < 99.50%: 35% credit
- Monthly credit cap: 30% of the monthly invoice (we can discuss increasing to 50% for longer-term committed contracts).
- Stability buffer: 0.20% of uptime is carved out for scheduled maintenance windows and rolling platform upgrades; we will provide a monthly maintenance log.
- Latency: we can guarantee p95 < 300ms for Dedicated customers. For Hosted, we commit to best-effort p95 targets and provide per-token latency telemetry (we will publish regional p95 numbers in the Console).
- Exceptions: credits excluded for customer-caused issues, force majeure, and agreed maintenance. Any planned maintenance > 4 hours in a calendar month will be notified at least 72 hours in advance.

Other notes:
- We prefer a single monthly credit line and automated reconciliation via your billing contacts (we included a HubSpot link in the draft so finance can wire to the invoice).
- We included an optional escalation playbook for throughput-containment incidents (fast-failover to a compatible model variant) to minimize customer impact.

Next steps: 1) Review the attached SLA draft, 2) let us know if your legal needs different wording on cap/cash-out, and 3) if you want the Dedicated latency guarantee, we can include pricing for a dedicated pool.

Subject: Fwd: Service assurance: minimum uptime & monthly credit construct

Ben / Laura — quick notes before I get back to FinApps: 

- FinApps will push to 99.9% and a credit cap = 100% of monthly spend. I think we can hold to 30% cap for hosted; consider 50% only for >12mo term or committed monthly spend.
- Offer: 99.95% hosted baseline with a 0.20% stability buffer for scheduled maintenance; offer Dedicated p95 < 300ms guarantee at a TCV uplift (need pricing).
- Legal points to prebake: definition of "unavailable" (we use failed request rate across region + internal retries), measurement window, and credit calculation math (we multiply downtime fraction by monthly invoice). Make sure maintenance notification SLA (72h) is explicit.
- For Finance: propose a single simple credit line and an auto-apply on next invoice; FinApps prefers that for reconciliation.

I'll propose the above to Sabrina and attach the redlined PDF. If we want to concede cap to 40% instead of 30% I recommend Ben lead pricing tradeoffs.

-Maya

Maya — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. The structure you proposed is clear and aligns with our procurement team’s needs. A few follow-ups from legal/procurement: 

1) Cap — procurement will accept a 30% monthly credit cap for the pilot/first year if we get a clear escalation SLA and a quarterly recap of incidents.
2) Maintenance carveout — please add an explicit example in the SLA showing how the 0.20% stability buffer maps to weekly/quarterly windows so legal can validate the carveout language.
3) Latency — we’ll take the Dedicated option for p95 < 300ms for the core inference path; please share pricing for a 3-node dedicated pool.
4) Invoice reconciliation — confirm you will auto-apply credits on the subsequent month’s invoice and provide a CSV export of credited line items.

If you can incorporate the sample carveout language and pricing, legal is ready to run a limited redline. Once those items are in the draft we’ll send to our GC.

Thanks —
Sabrina

Sabrina Lowe
Head of Procurement, FinApps
